# How to Ask MiniMax Code to Build a Checklist Web Page You Can Open

> **In short:** You describe the checklist you want in plain words, MiniMax Code builds it as a small web page file, and you open that file in your browser. Ask it to save ticked items, then test that they stay ticked after you reload. The help article doesn't say where saved files appear, so check the official help center for details.

You'll learn how to turn an everyday idea, like a checklist that remembers what you already ticked off, into a small web page you can open on your own computer. No coding is needed. This guide is for anyone who has never built a web page and wants a practical first try.

## Before you start

- **MiniMax Code**, installed and open on your computer. The help article describes a desktop-style app with a sidebar and a message box at the bottom.
- **A folder on your computer** where the finished file can go. You will choose it as your workspace.
- **Some patience.** Plan on about 20 to 30 minutes for the first try, including testing.
- **Plan check:** the official help article doesn't say whether any plan limits this feature, so look on the official MiniMax website for current details.

## Step 1 — Start a new task

Start a new task in MiniMax Code. Look for a **New Task** option in the sidebar. You can also type straight into the message box on the home screen, which the help article calls the home composer. Either way, you are opening a fresh task, which is the basic unit of work in this app, a bit like starting a new project folder for one job.

When you do this, you should see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom of the screen. Nothing has been built yet, and that is normal. If your screen looks different, for example the sidebar is hidden, look for a small menu or icon that opens it, or check the official help center for the exact layout on your device.

💬 Example: New task, then type the next step's prompt in the message box.

You'll know it worked when you have a fresh, empty task ready for your request.

## Step 2 — Describe the page you want

This is the most important step. Describe the result you want, not every click. The help article says that asking for an outcome, such as "build a page", is the right way to start. For coding tasks, it also suggests including the technology, any limits you care about, and how you will check the result.

Keep it simple. You don't need technical words. Say what the page shows, what should happen when you tick an item, and that you want one file you can open in a browser. Write it as if you were explaining to a friend.

💬 Example: "Build a simple web page with a checklist of [number] grocery items. Each item has a box I can tick. The page should remember which boxes are ticked after I reload it. Save everything as one HTML file that I can open in my web browser."

You'll know it worked when your request is in the message box and you can read it back clearly. If it feels too long, cut it down to the outcome and one or two important details.

## Step 3 — Add the context

Next, tell MiniMax Code where to work. The help article says you can select a workspace, which is the folder the Agent uses. Choose the folder you prepared earlier. You can also drag in files, or mention a project file with an @ symbol, if you already have files you want it to look at. If you have none, skip this part.

Look for a control near the message box that lets you select a workspace or attach context. The exact label may vary, so if you can't find it, look for something that mentions a folder or project. Then add one line to your request naming the folder's purpose, for example "Save the file in my checklist folder."

💬 Example: "Put the finished file in the folder I selected, and name it checklist.html."

You'll know it worked when the folder you chose appears as the workspace for this task.

## Step 4 — Speak your request instead of typing (optional)

If typing is slow for you, MiniMax Code has voice input. Look for the **microphone** in the bottom-right corner of the message box. The first time you use it, the app will ask permission to use your microphone. Allow it. Then speak your request in a normal voice. Your words appear as text in the box as you talk.

You can edit the text before sending. To send it right away, the help article says you can click **Transcribe and send** while recording. If you want to choose a different microphone, go to **Settings → Voice → Microphone**. Keyboard shortcuts for dictation live in **Settings → Voice → Dictation**, and none is set by default.

If you don't see the microphone, check your device settings and the official help center. Typing works just as well, so you can skip this step.

💬 Example: Say, "Build a simple checklist web page that remembers my ticks."

You'll know it worked when your spoken words appear in the message box and you can read them before you send.

## Step 5 — Send it and answer the prompts

Send your request. The Agent starts working, and you may see progress as it goes. The help article notes that you can add more requirements while it works, and you may be asked for permission at some point. Read each prompt before you respond. If it asks to create or change a file in your chosen folder, that is expected for this task. If something looks unrelated, decline and ask for what you actually want.

When it finishes, read its summary. If the reply doesn't mention where the file is, ask directly. The help article doesn't describe where saved files appear, so the official help center is the place to confirm details.

💬 Example: "Please tell me the full file name and the folder where you saved it."

You'll know it worked when the Agent reports that the task is done and names the file it created.

## Step 6 — Open the page in your browser and test it

Find the HTML file in the folder you chose. On most computers, double-clicking a file ending in .html opens it in your web browser. If that doesn't work, right-click the file and choose a browser from the open-with menu.

Now test it. Tick three boxes, then reload or close and reopen the page. If the ticks are still there, the memory feature works. If they disappear, don't panic. Go back to the task and describe what happened.

💬 Example: "When I tick two items and reload the page, the ticks disappear. Please fix it so the checked items are saved."

You'll know it worked when your ticks stay after you reload the page.

## Common mistakes

- **Describing steps instead of the result.** Saying "add a div, then a button" makes things harder. Describe the checklist you want, and MiniMax Code can handle the building. Fix it by writing the outcome first.
- **Skipping the test.** A page can look right but not remember ticks. Fix it by reloading the page after ticking boxes, and asking for a change if it fails.
- **Assuming it's finished when the reply sounds confident.** Always open the file and check. If something is missing, say exactly what, for example "the ticks don't save."

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** make a packing list for a trip, a weekly chore chart, or a grocery checklist you can open on your computer.
- **For your business or work:** build a simple internal checklist, such as a setup or onboarding list, as one file a colleague can open.
- **If you're just getting started:** ask for one small page with three checkboxes, then add one feature at a time.

Honest limit: MiniMax Code can build a page and write the instructions for it, but it cannot promise the page behaves perfectly in every browser or on every device. Test it yourself before relying on it.

## Try it now

Open MiniMax Code, start a new task, and type: "Build a simple web page with a checklist of [number] items. Each item has a box I can tick. Save it as one HTML file." Then open the file in your browser and tick two boxes.
